rows.forYouRules: Built from your ratings, Favourites, Like and Not interested marks, what you finished and what you dropped; recent ones count more. Candidates: what's recommended for your titles, what's watched with them on Lumovio (only with five accounts or more, no names), work by your directors and actors, new titles in your genres and copies on your servers. Ordered by how well they fit your taste, ratings weighed by their votes, and how new they are; the first cards come from different franchises and genres. Left out: what you watched, rated, started, queued, hid or muted. Only this profile's data is used, and nothing is sent to AI services.

method.title: Lumovio Score
method.what: Lumovio Score is Lumovio's own derived score from 0 to 100. It is a percentile: 87 means the title is rated higher than 87% of films (or of series, for a series).
method.scale: Every source's score is placed on one scale, IMDb's: the reference is the IMDb ratings of the titles Lumovio knows that have at least 1,000 votes in IMDb's dataset, separately for films and series. Each other source is linked to it through titles rated by both, at least 200 per source and kind; a source with fewer is left out until there are more. TMDB is linked through a weekly sample of its most-voted titles, of which only the resulting table is kept. The tables are rebuilt every week.
method.weights: Few votes pull a source towards the middle: it counts in full only with many votes or reviews. Audiences — IMDb, Letterboxd (films only), TMDB, Rotten Tomatoes' Popcornmeter, Trakt and MyAnimeList — make up 60% of the score; critics — the Tomatometer and Metacritic, equally — 40%. For the first 30 days after release, audience scores need twice the votes. Each score counts once, whoever delivered it, and a missing score is never a zero.
method.shown: Cards show the score only at medium or high confidence. The title page also shows a low one, marked “Few ratings”, notes “Opinions differ” when Critics and Audience are 20 or more points apart, and its “How it's calculated” lists every source with its share of the weight and the sources left out.
method.terms: TVmaze (CC BY-SA) and AniList are not part of it under their terms; their scores are still shown. Every source's own score stays on its own chip, with its logo, date and link.
method.derived: Lumovio Score is a derived score by Lumovio. None of the services whose scores it uses — IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, Letterboxd, Trakt, MyAnimeList and TMDB — publishes or endorses it. Methodology version {version}.

devUi.deleteServerText: The files stay on the server; Lumovio stops showing them.
devUi.confirmTyped: The most dangerous, and typing text

devUi.nothingDeleted: This is the showcase: nothing was deleted

devUi.toastNote: Bottom centre, above the tab bar on a phone. A status icon, one line, an optional action for any tone.

devUi.alertNote: A banner in a page or panel: the status's soft fill, an icon, a title, text and one action at the end. No coloured frame.

devUi.skeletonNote: Repeats the final layout — the same card and row sizes; shimmers every 1.6 s, still with reduced motion.
devUi.progressNote: 4 px, filled with --progress; an unknown length runs a stripe.
devUi.step2: Loading the start of the file
devUi.step3error: The server didn't answer. Retry or pick another source.
devUi.emptyNote: An icon in a circle, a title, up to two lines of text, one main button and an optional link. Empty shelves aren't shown at all.

devUi.errorNote: Words, mark and Retry chosen by the error (lib/api-errors): no connection, a failure, a limit — no Retry where it can't help. Why it happened is for a screen reader; technical details only on a page.
devUi.queryNote: Loading → skeleton, error → ErrorState with a retry, empty → EmptyState, data → the content; a failed refresh keeps the data and offers a retry. An error never looks like “empty”.
devUi.brandLoaderNote: While a page or a video stream is awaited: light passes from the projector to the screen, a 1.6 s loop. A page shows it after 300 ms of waiting, under the header; the player on the stage. A button's action keeps its small spinner, a layout its skeleton.

devUi.brandActionsNote: The heart of Favourites, the thumb of “Like”, the star of a rating — once, when the server has confirmed: in the “Added to Favourites” toast the mark draws in full, on a button whose outline is already there only the fill and a light settle play. devUi.settingsNote: A panel with a title and rows. A switch applies at once, “Saved” appears by the title; a failure rolls back and leaves an alert in the section with a retry.
devUi.setSectionDesc: Applies on every device of this profile.
devUi.setFailDesc: The next requests fail with a network error
devUi.actionNote: useAction: the row goes at once; if the server refuses, it comes back and a toast says what failed; Undo in the toast brings it back. A failure can't be swallowed.

connectionHelp.title: Help with connecting
connectionHelp.description: How Lumovio reaches your server, and what to do when it can't.
connectionHelp.address_jellyfin: The address you open Jellyfin at in a browser, with its port: http://192.168.1.10:8096 or https://jellyfin.example.com.
connectionHelp.address_torrserver: The address of TorrServer's web page, with its port (8090 unless you changed it): http://192.168.1.10:8090. If TorrServer asks for a password, enter that login.
connectionHelp.address_plex: No address needed: sign in with Plex, and Lumovio uses the server's address that answers from this device — Plex's own HTTPS addresses (plex.direct) first.
connectionHelp.lnaTitle: A server at home: the browser's question
connectionHelp.lnaAsk: Chrome and Edge ask whether Lumovio may connect to devices on your local network. Choose “Allow”.
connectionHelp.lnaBlocked: If you chose “Block”: click the icon left of the address → Site settings → Local network access → Allow, then check the server again.
connectionHelp.lnaOthers: Safari and Firefox don't ask: they block http:// addresses on a secure page. Use the server's HTTPS address there.
connectionHelp.httpsWhen: An HTTPS address works in every browser and on every device, at home and away. Ways to get one:
connectionHelp.httpsTailscale: Tailscale Serve: on the server's computer, run {command}. The address it gives ends in .ts.net; your devices need Tailscale on.
connectionHelp.httpsProxy: A reverse proxy with a real certificate (Caddy, Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik) on your own domain.
connectionHelp.httpsPlex: Turn on Remote Access in the Plex server's settings. Its plex.direct addresses are HTTPS already.
connectionHelp.tip_jellyfin: Behind a reverse proxy, let Jellyfin's CORS headers through, or the browser refuses its answers.
connectionHelp.tip_torrserver: Lumovio works with MatriX builds of TorrServer. If the check says the server refused this site, update TorrServer.
connectionHelp.tip_plex: If no server answers, open Plex on that computer and check that it's signed in to the same Plex account.
connectionHelp.stepServerOn: Check that the server is on and its program is running.
connectionHelp.stepOpenAddress: Open {address} in a new tab on this device. If it doesn't open there either, this device can't reach the server.
connectionHelp.stepSameNetwork: Away from home, the server answers only through Tailscale or an address on the internet.
connectionHelp.stepLnaAllow: In Chrome or Edge, allow access to your local network when the browser asks.
connectionHelp.stepUseHttps: In other browsers, and away from home, use the server's HTTPS address: Tailscale Serve or a reverse proxy.
connectionHelp.stepCertificate: This device doesn't trust the address's certificate (a self-signed one, say). Use a real one: Tailscale Serve, or Let's Encrypt in your reverse proxy.
connectionHelp.stepSignIn: Check the username and password. For a server you've added, sign in again in “Change address and sign-in”.
connectionHelp.stepTailnet: A name ending in .ts.net answers only while Tailscale is on on this device.
connectionHelp.stepRestart: Restart the server and check again.
